findings.reason: The protected implementation repeatedly uses the explicitly prohibited local name `index`. The inert candidate preserves the exact accepted active-frontier algorithm and app-local `solve(arr)` contract while replacing loop positions with conventional interview notation `i` and `j`. This is the smallest material correction required by the repository's expert-review naming standard; the protected app source, immutable native source, and verified submission remain untouched.

The candidate is concise, direct, and explainable. `values` makes input preservation visible, `active` names the only positions requiring reevaluation, `changes` separates read-only evaluation from the simultaneous write batch, and `i`, `j`, and `delta` are conventional local notation. It introduces no abstraction, mutable global state, code golf, or incidental behavior.

Every active position is classified using the unchanged current array, and all signed changes are applied only after classification finishes, so each day is simultaneous. Initially every interior position is active. After a batch, only a changed position or one of its neighbors can have a different three-value neighborhood; the next frontier contains exactly those interior candidates. Any omitted position therefore remains non-extreme. When the active frontier yields no changes, no interior position can change, while the endpoints were never eligible.

The initial scan evaluates `O(n)` positions. Every actual increment or decrement contributes at most three positions to the next frontier, so the candidate performs `O(n+C)` evaluations over the whole process, where `C` is the total number of element updates. Copies, change records, and frontier membership require `O(n)` space.
